product: Fresh strawberries (Fragaria x ananassa), packed for refrigerated truck transport
not_a_drug_label: This is FOOD handling guidance, not a pharmaceutical label. Nothing here is a regulatory storage statement and none of it has been through any medicines-regulator review. Do not read a verdict computed against this profile as pharmaceutical validation of anything.
source: USDA Agriculture Handbook 66, 'The Commercial Storage of Fruits, Vegetables, and Florist and Nursery Stocks' — Strawberry commodity summary (p. 560)
verified_note: PDF downloaded from ars.usda.gov and read directly on 2026-08-28 (3,762,512 bytes). Strawberry summary, 'Optimum Storage Conditions', verbatim: 'Store at 0 °C (32 °F) with 90 to 95% RH. Strawberry fruit can be stored for up to 7 days at 0 °C (32 °F), depending on disease pressure.' Same summary, 'Chilling Sensitivity', verbatim: 'Strawberry fruit are not sensitive to chilling and should be stored as cold as possible without freezing.' UC Davis Postharvest's Produce Facts sheet for strawberry was also sought as a second source but postharvest.ucdavis.edu returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) on 2026-08-28, so nothing from it is cited here.
storage_min_provenance: Published figure. 0 °C is the storage temperature AH-66 states outright for strawberry, and the dataset's own paper (arXiv:2103.12895) describes the shipments as precooled to 0 °C, so the band floor matches both the guidance and the operating set point of the trailers that produced this data.
storage_max_provenance: BENCHMARK ASSUMPTION, not a published figure. AH-66 gives strawberry an optimum (0 °C) but no upper limit of acceptability, so no source says 'store at 0 to 4 °C'. 4 °C is chosen as the ceiling because (a) AH-66's respiration table for strawberry shows 12-20 mg CO2 kg-1 h-1 at 0 °C against 50-100 at 10 °C, so deterioration is already several-fold faster before 10 °C is reached; (b) AH-66 notes Rhizopus stolonifer 'cannot grow at temperatures <5 °C (41 °F)', which puts a spoilage-relevant boundary just above 4 °C; and (c) the risk labelling published alongside this dataset by its own mirror uses >4 °C (its 'dur_gt4' feature) as the elevated-temperature threshold. A real quality system would set this from its own shelf-life data.
excursion_envelope: Deliberately not set. The pharmaceutical idea of a permitted excursion envelope around a labelled band (as on the openFDA amoxicillin label this project's other profile uses) has no counterpart in produce handling guidance: AH-66 states one recommended temperature, not an outer envelope. Setting excursion_min_c/excursion_max_c here would mean inventing a second published band that does not exist, so the profile leaves them out and the verdict rests on the storage band plus the configured time allowance.
freeze_rule_note: ColdCall's default freeze rule disqualifies any time below storage_min_c. For strawberry that would be wrong, and config.json therefore sets no_freeze_rule: AH-66 says strawberries 'are not sensitive to chilling and should be stored as cold as possible without freezing', so a probe reading -0.3 °C is nearer to correct practice than one reading +3.0 °C, and treating it as a disqualifying freeze would condemn well-run shipments on a fraction of a degree. Time below 0 °C is still counted as out-of-band and still consumes the excursion allowance; only the automatic disqualification is off. AH-66's strawberry summary does not state the fruit's freezing point, so no freezing-point figure is asserted anywhere in this adapter.
